title: The Final Ledger
premise: August Ravensworth, a night dispatcher who solves cold cases as a hobby, receives two letters about the unsolved 1989 Ravensworth Hotel fire: one confessing to arson and murder, one promising the truth if August can find the sender's hidden ledger before the police do. As August investigates, they discover the letters were written by their presumed-dead mother, whose identity was stolen decades ago, and that the current Ravensworth estate heirs are covering up a second, ongoing murder. In the end, August traps the killer — their mother's old business partner, now the family lawyer — by feeding him a falsified ledger page, forcing a confession recorded live, and learns their mother died protecting the original evidence rather than destroying it.
about_author: Rafael Yarrow is the pen name of a former insurance fraud investigator turned novelist who spent fifteen years reading other people's lies on paper. They write mysteries from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Maine coast, where the fog does half the editing.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Postmark
chapters.summary: August Ravensworth, working the graveyard shift at Crescent Cab, opens two letters about the 1989 Ravensworth Hotel fire — one a confession, one a taunt promising 'the ledger holds the rest.' Both are signed with August's own childhood nickname. POV: August. Emotional beat: uneasy recognition, the past knocking at a door August thought was sealed.

chapters.title: The Fire Nobody Finished
chapters.summary: August digs into the fire that killed three people, including a woman listed only as 'M. Vale,' and finds the official report riddled with gaps — pages missing, a witness statement dated after the witness died. POV: August, intercut with the 1989 report excerpts. Emotional beat: the thrill of a case that finally bites back.

chapters.title: The Heirs of Ravensworth
chapters.summary: August visits the rebuilt Ravensworth estate under pretense of a cab company audit and meets the heirs: matriarch Eleanor, her nervous son Daniel, and family lawyer Corwin Hale, whose charm has a rehearsed edge. Someone watches August from an upstairs window. POV: August. Emotional beat: the wrongness of a house that smiles too easily.

chapters.title: A Name That Was Borrowed
chapters.summary: A retired archivist reveals 'M. Vale' was an alias — and the handwriting samples match letters August's mother sent before vanishing in 1988. August's mother didn't die in the fire; she may have started it, or been running from whoever did. POV: August. Emotional beat: grief reassembling itself around a stranger who was always family.

chapters.title: The Second Body
chapters.summary: Daniel's business partner is found drowned in the estate pond, ruled accidental — but the timeline mirrors the 1989 fire exactly. August realizes the pattern is repeating and that the letters' sender knew it would. POV: August, with a brief shift to Daniel's panicked perspective. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Ledger Pages and Lies
chapters.summary: August finds half a hidden ledger in the hotel's old safe-deposit records: accounts showing the fire was insurance fraud, with initials 'C.H.' beside the payouts. Corwin Hale's name. But the ledger is too easy to find — someone wanted it discovered. POV: August. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing the trail is a leash.

chapters.title: What the Confessor Confessed
chapters.summary: August traces the letters' paper and typewriter ribbon to the estate itself and confronts Eleanor, who admits writing them — she found her husband's old ledger and wanted the family's rot exposed before she dies, but she isn't the killer. POV: Eleanor's confession in her voice, framed by August. Emotional beat: an ally found in the last place August looked.

chapters.title: The Night Shift Trap
chapters.summary: August stages a fake discovery: a completed ledger page naming Hale's current fraud scheme, 'found' at the cab depot and leaked to Daniel. Hale must come for it himself. August works the night shift as bait, radios open, the depot lights rigged to fail. POV: August. Emotional beat: cold, controlled fear — the dispatcher becomes the dispatch.

chapters.title: Corwin Hale's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Hale breaks in, and August records his confession: he killed August's mother in 1989 when she threatened to expose the fraud, and killed Daniel's partner last week for the same reason. Hale realizes the trap too late; police, tipped by August, arrive as he tries to burn the real ledger. POV: alternating August and Hale. Emotional beat: the climax's terrible clarity — a man who only ever counted.

chapters.title: Closing the Account
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, August reads their mother's final letter, hidden in the ledger's spine: she stayed silent to protect August, and died trying to come home. The case closes, the heirs begin to rebuild honestly, and August pins the last page above the dispatch desk. POV: August. Emotional beat: mourning and inheritance reconciled — some ledgers balance in blood, some in truth.
